title: A Mathematical Theory of Evolutionary Economics
affiliations: Yunnan Province Library

detail.title: A Mathematical Theory of Evolutionary Economics
detail.abstract: The economy is an integral part of the social system. Society is a group-level structure. Group selection is trapped in the altruistic dilemma. This paper defines the existence of an evolutionary subject as a non-homogeneous Markov process. Fitness is the logarithm of the probability of death of the subject. Pure altruism and kin altruism are essentially the same, i.e., dependency. The reward for an individual's payment of fitness is not material, but rather an increase in their own fitness through an increase in the fitness of the other. Based on dependency theory, the conditions of primitive communism are proven. This paper constructs the basic principles of evolutionary market economics: when the value produced by society is insufficient, the price of the commodity is determined by value, and the supply-demand ratio causes the price to deviate from value. When there is excess production in society, the price of the commodity is determined by utility and value, and the supply-demand ratio causes the price to deviate.

title: Macroeconomic shocks and long-term nutritional outcomes: Insights from the Asian financial crisis
affiliations: University of Bonn - Center for Development Research (ZEF) and University of Bonn

detail.title: Macroeconomic shocks and long-term nutritional outcomes: Insights from the Asian financial crisis
detail.abstract: Climate change, conflicts, pandemics, and other disruptive events can lead to shocks in people’s incomes, prices, and access to food, with profound implications for nutrition and health. The short- and long-term effects of different types of shocks are not yet sufficiently understood. Here, we use data from Indonesia to analyze effects of the Asian financial crisis, which happened in the late-1990s, on nutritional outcomes. The crisis contributed to large temporary increases in rice prices with regional variation, which we exploit to estimate effects on child height-for-age z-scores (HAZ) and other anthropometric indicators. Panel data regression models with individual fixed effects suggest that the rice price inflation led to an average decrease in HAZ of 0.16 and an increase in child stunting by 4 percentage points, after controlling for confounding factors. These effects are more pronounced in urban than rural areas. Children with mothers that only have little education suffer over-proportionally. Beyond the immediate impacts, we examine long-term effects and find that individuals severely hit by the crisis during childhood remain shorter also during adulthood and are more likely to be obese. Our findings highlight the need for nutrition-sensitive interventions in national and global crisis response policies.

title: Severe Weather and Collateral Practices
affiliations: Sveriges Riksbank and

detail.title: Severe Weather and Collateral Practices
detail.abstract: Physical climate risks significantly influence banks' collateral practices. Drawing on comprehensive loan-level data from Sweden, we find that adverse weather events increase both the likelihood and the amount of collateral required for new loans. In the case of existing loans, banks are less inclined to reappraise collateral following weather shocks; when reappraisals do occur, collateral values tend to be revised downward. Our analysis also underscores the mitigating effect of proximity between borrowers and lenders in this context. Furthermore, we find that extreme weather events do not directly affect banks' one-year default probability assessments.

title: Evaluation of High Rate MBBR to Predict Optimal Design Parameters for Higher Carbon and Subsequent Ammoniacal Nitrogen Removal
affiliations: and Thermax Limited

detail.title: Evaluation of High Rate MBBR to Predict Optimal Design Parameters for Higher Carbon and Subsequent Ammoniacal Nitrogen Removal
detail.abstract: The high rate moving bed biofilm reactor (MBBR) processes were designed for wastewater treatment to meet the past effluent discharge norms of biological oxygen demand (BOD) <50 mg/l. However, they are incapable of meeting current effluent discharge norms which consist of BOD <10 mg/l and total nitrogen <10 mg/l. This study analyses the effect and variation of organic loading rate from 1.21 kg to 4.59 kg chemical oxygen demand (COD)/(m3.day) and surface loading rate from 4.9 g to 24 g COD/(m2. day) on a high rate MBBR performance. The results of COD reduction (CODred) and subsequent ammoniacal nitrogen reduction (NH3–Nred) were in the range of 65.4% to 87.8% and 11.8% to 47.2% respectively. The projected graphical optimization defines the design parameters for MBBR and also predicts CODred and subsequent NH3–Nred. By understanding this subsequent NH3–Nred in the MBBR system, future designs for engineering technologies will be aided.

title: The Geoeconomic Role of Sovereign Wealth Funds: Effects on Global Trade
affiliations: UCLA Anderson School of Management and

detail.title: The Geoeconomic Role of Sovereign Wealth Funds: Effects on Global Trade
detail.abstract: Sovereign wealth funds (SWFs) have emerged as potent instruments of geoeconomic strategy. Using comprehensive data on 2,362 private-market deals by 43 SWFs (1999-2022), we show that an initial SWF investment increases home-country exports by 8.2%-equivalent to $0.11 in annual exports per dollar invested. These gains concentrate in manufacturing and technology exports from developing to advanced economies, inverting the conventional trade hierarchy. Causal identification exploits the 2018 U.S. Foreign Investment Risk Review Modernization Act: more-exposed SWFs significantly redirected capital to non-U.S. destinations, generating a subsequent boost in exports to those markets. Crucially, we find no crowd-out of other exporters, indicating net trade creation. Results demonstrate that SWFs facilitate trade by reducing market-access frictions and providing political-risk insurance, not by alleviating financing constraints.

title: Climate Change and Renewable Energy: How to Choose the Optimal Pool of Technologies
affiliations: Environment Europe Foundation

detail.title: Climate Change and Renewable Energy: How to Choose the Optimal Pool of Technologies
detail.abstract: Renewable energy is seen as an alternative to conventional energy sources, which are predominantly fossil-fuel based and cause dangerous climate change. Various forms of renewable energy also require some resource inputs and installations need to be replaced every 30 years or so. This leads an analyst to the problem of careful selection of a pool of energy sources. Although the conventional form of analysis has largely been centred on cost-minimization, more and more additional criteria, belonging to the economic, social, technical, risk, resource and emissions realms are introduced to make justifi ed decisions on the selection of one technology or of one combination over the other. This chapter makes the fi rst step towards this goal by providing taxonomy of criteria used in decision making regarding renewable energy; it also reviews existing modelling approaches which are currently used in the fi eld. Methodologically, the emphasis in this chapter is on multicriteria decision aid tools.

title: Talk and the City: How Far to Trust Bankers (Not) Calling for Bailouts?
affiliations: University of Greifswald - Department of Economics and University of Vienna

detail.title: Talk and the City: How Far to Trust Bankers (Not) Calling for Bailouts?
detail.abstract: To evaluate a bank's resilience to financial stress, authorities often rely on private information from a peer institution, or counterparty. This reliance can be perilous, especially when assessing bailout options. Within a global games approach to bank runs, we study communication about a systemically important bank's financial status between an informed counterparty of said bank and an uninformed authority. This communication is costless, non-binding, and unverifiable-and yet pivotal for the authority's decision to bailout the bank. When information about the counterparty's own liquidity needs is private, the counterparty may exaggerate the systemically important bank's true need for support, but it may also withhold adverse information entirely. We show that the authority's risks in assessing bailout options is (1) shaped by the strategic behavior of the informed counterparty, (2) dependent on knowledge of the counterparty's own financial position, and (3) not necessarily continuous.

title: Stock Grants, Tax Incentives, and Fiduciary Reality: A Reappraisal of Voluntary Equity Distribution
affiliations: Mercer

detail.title: Stock Grants, Tax Incentives, and Fiduciary Reality: A Reappraisal of Voluntary Equity Distribution
detail.abstract: This paper offers a structural critique of voluntary broad based equity distribution programs that rely on tax incentives or credits to encourage employer adoption. While such proposals have gained attention among policymakers and academics, the analysis shows that they are unlikely to scale into durable ownership institutions. Using financial modeling, board governance standards, and fiduciary obligations, the paper demonstrates why one time tax benefits do not create lasting firm value, why dilution limits constrain corporate willingness to issue new shares, and why voluntary equity cannot satisfy fiduciary duties to existing shareholders. The discussion contrasts these limits with Employee Stock Ownership Plans, which function as regulated retirement trusts and have produced significant wealth and stability for rank and file workers over decades. Case evidence from ESPPs, RSUs, broad grant cultures, and private equity contingent equity programs illustrates both the reach and the limits of non fiduciary approaches. The paper concludes by outlining five structural pathways that can extend ownership at scale, including modernized ESOP safe harbors, hybrid trust models, fairer RSU and ESPP designs, and a temporal framework for aligning equity instruments with appropriate horizons. The argument positions fiduciary and trust based structures as the only viable path to build durable broad based employee ownership at retirement scale.

title: Dynamic Capabilities and Entrepreneurial Management in Large Organizations: Toward a Theory of the (Entrepreneurial) Firm
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley - Business & Public Policy Group

detail.title: Dynamic Capabilities and Entrepreneurial Management in Large Organizations: Toward a Theory of the (Entrepreneurial) Firm
detail.abstract: Mainstream economic theory has generally excluded consideration of the role of managers, which has, in turn, impaired its ability to explain resource allocation by, and heterogeneity among, firms. In the real world, managers are called on to fill entrepreneurial and leadership roles: sensing opportunities, developing and implementing viable business models, building capabilities, and guiding the organization through transformations. These entrepreneurial management tasks are part of the organization's capabilities, which also encompass embedded organizational processes that can be slow to change. An understanding of entrepreneurial management and organizational capabilities will contribute to more realistic economic models and a better understanding by policy makers of industrial dynamics and the requirements of innovation.

title: Comments to the Consultation Paper on Sustainability Reporting
affiliations: Nyenrode Business University, Nyenrode Business University and Nyenrode Business University

detail.title: Comments to the Consultation Paper on Sustainability Reporting

contentType.other: Comments to the Consultation Paper on Sustainability Reporting - Exposure Draft

detail.abstract:
We believe the timing of the publication of the document is fundamentally spot-on, as a reaction to societal demands, as well as to changed attitudes towards sustainability in the corporate sector and in the financial markets. On the other hand, we think the substantiation of the need for sustainability reporting within the document itself is not fully convincing, neither are the objectives of sustainability reporting made clear to the reader, nor the dilemmas facing alignment of the multiple objectives. Also, there is no clarity regarding the multiple audiences.
The search for relevant and purposeful sustainability reporting has been prevalent in [a specific branch of] accounting research during the last 30 years, but this research has been ignored in the consultation paper. We support this consultation, which may have to be changed into a pre-consultation, as this document may need further substantiation with relevant scholarly literature. We give some brief input for this.
Worthwhile mentioning is, that we take a European (EU) perspective.

title: Nigeria's Digital Assets Regulation and cNGN: A Dialogue Between Olayimika Oyebanji and the Representatives of the French Treasury
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Nigeria's Digital Assets Regulation and cNGN: A Dialogue Between Olayimika Oyebanji and the Representatives of the French Treasury
detail.abstract: This transcript captures a detailed conversation between Olayimika Oyebanji, a Nigerian-based blockchain lawyer and founder of Blocklaw Consulting, and representatives from the French Treasury(an Economic Department of the French Embassy in Nigeria), Carole Lebreton and Marwan Sabri. The meeting centers on the evolving landscape of cryptocurrency regulation in Nigeria, with particular focus on the implications of the Investment Securities Act of 2025, the classification of digital assets as securities, and the regulatory challenges facing the local crypto industry. Throughout the discussion, the participants explore the impact of these regulations on innovation, the hurdles faced by startups, and the broader economic context influencing cryptocurrency adoption in Nigeria. The conversation also delves into the introduction and critique of the cNGN stablecoin, drawing comparisons with global regulatory frameworks and highlighting the unique challenges of implementing a Naira-backed stablecoin. This transcript offers valuable insights into the intersection of law, policy, and technology in one of Africa's most dynamic crypto markets, making it a useful resource for students, researchers, and professionals interested in digital finance and regulatory affairs.

title: Italian Electricity Market Forecasting and Time-Series Synchrony Analysis: Interim Study I
affiliations: University of Bari, University of Naples, University of Bari and Tecnalogic Srl

detail.title: Italian Electricity Market Forecasting and Time-Series Synchrony Analysis: Interim Study I
detail.abstract: In this study, we analyze forecasting performance in the Italian electricity market with a focus on day-ahead (MGP) and current-day (MDS) forecasts of hourly energy demand. Our approach builds on a discrete-time approximation of a Vasicek-type stochastic differential equation (SDE), driven by skew Brownian motion and a compound Poisson process, to capture both asymmetric fluctuations and sudden imbalances. Forecast accuracy is assessed through goodness of fit measures (RMSE, NMSE, IDX) and by evaluating time-series synchrony using peak/trough alignment, cross-correlation, dynamic time warping (DTW), coherence, and instantaneous phase synchrony (IPS). Preliminary results based on January 2024 hourly data indicate that the model achieves improved alignment between forecasts and actual demand, with reductions in forecasting errors and a more robust representation of variability across temporal scales.

title: Do Mortgage Lender Incentives Distort Refinancing Likelihood?
affiliations: and University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School

detail.title: Do Mortgage Lender Incentives Distort Refinancing Likelihood?
detail.abstract: Homeowners can save thousands of dollars by refinancing when mortgage rates fall, yet many "in-the-money" borrowers do not refinance. Non-portfolio lenders that rely on fee income have stronger incentives to promote refinancing than portfolio lenders that rely on interest payments. We document supply-side distortions in refinancing by exploiting a 2020 conforming loan limit (CLL) increase that generated exogenous variation in lender incentives for some jumbo mortgages. The increase in CLL with scheduled amortization meant some jumbo loans became eligible for conforming refinance, and thus gained access to non-portfolio lenders. Refinancing increases by 27% for these eligible jumbo loans. Our identification strategy provides the first causal estimate of supply-side incentive frictions in mortgage refinancing.

title: A Case for AXI
affiliations: Cornell University - Department of Economics

detail.title: A Case for AXI

declarations.funderStatement: Viktor Tsyrennikov gratefully acknowledges financial and data support from SOFR Academy, Inc.

detail.abstract:
In the LIBOR era, banks routinely tied revolving credit facilities to credit-sensitive benchmarks. This study assesses the Across-the-Curve Credit Spread Index (AXI)-a transparent, transaction-based measure of wholesale bank funding costs-as a complement to SOFR, summarizing its behavior, construction, and loan-pricing implications. AXI aggregates observable unsecured funding transactions across short-and long-term maturities to produce a daily credit spread that is IOSCO-aligned and operationally compatible with SOFR-based infrastructure.
The Financial Conditions Credit Spread Index (FXI) is a broader market companion to AXI and serves as its fallback. FXI co-moves closely with AXI in normal times; under stress, the correlation of daily changes exceeds 0.9 for economy-wide shocks and remains strong in bank-specific stress, around 0.8 during the Silicon Valley Bank episode.
Empirically, AXI is strongly correlated with standard credit-spread measures and market-stress indicators and is inversely related to financial sector performance. SOFR+AXI exhibits correlations with macroeconomic variables with the signs and magnitudes expected of a credit-sensitive rate. In loan-pricing applications, SOFR+AXI reduces funding risk and can support spread discounts of up to 65 basis points without lowering risk-adjusted returns. In stress scenarios, banks relying on SOFR-only pricing can fail to recover as much as 15 basis points on revolving credit lines over as little as three months.
Taken together, AXI restores the credit sensitivity lost in the USD LIBOR transition while avoiding reliance on thin short-term markets, delivering significant economic value.

title: Electronic Transfer Taxes and the Stock Market: Empirical Evidence from Ghana’s E-Levy
affiliations: , Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) and Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU)

detail.title: Electronic Transfer Taxes and the Stock Market: Empirical Evidence from Ghana’s E-Levy
detail.abstract: This paper aims to highlight the correlation between Ghana's Electronic Transfer Levy (E-levy) and the stock market performance of the target firms. Initially, the E-levy aimed to raise GH₵7 billion by taxing electronic transfers exceeding GH₵100 daily at a rate of 1.75%. Following a rate reduction to 1.5%, the revenue target was revised to GH₵4.5 billion. Using a difference-indifferences approach, we find a negative effect on target firm stock prices, persisting around the implementation period. We also find that reducing the levy influences stock prices positively. Our channel test reveals that the levy affects the stock market through transaction volume, with a stronger result for firms with below-average trading volumes. The policy recommendation is to reduce the rate below 0.5%. IMPACT STATEMENT This study provides critical empirical insights into the correlation between Ghana's Electronic Transfer Levy (E-Levy) and the stock market performance of targeted firms, notably fintech companies and banks. Employing a robust difference-indifferences analytical approach, it reveals that the introduction of the levy negatively correlated with stock prices, primarily through reduced trading volumes, particularly affecting firms with lower-than-average trading activities. The research underscores significant market sensitivity to fiscal policy adjustments, highlighting the importance of carefully designing tax frameworks. The findings advocate for policy reconsideration, notably suggesting either cancellation or further reductions in the E-Levy rate to mitigate adverse market responses and enhance financial market stability and investor confidence in Ghana.

title: Partial Cartels and Ringleaders: An Experimental Study
affiliations: University of Potsdam, University of Göttingen and

detail.title: Partial Cartels and Ringleaders: An Experimental Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: This research is funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) – project number 389447910, and by the Wissenschaftsraum Behavioral Economics and Societal Transformation through the zukunft.niedersachsen program (Volkswagen Foundation and Lower Saxony Ministry of Science and Culture), which we gratefully acknowledge.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates partial cartels, which laboratory studies have neglected despite their empirical prevalence. We conduct two laboratory experiments to understand how they function compared to all-inclusive cartels and respond to antitrust policies. First, we compare partial cartel formation with all-inclusive settings typically studied experimentally. Second, we test how ringleader discrimination policies perform within partial cartel environments. Our first study reveals that partial cartels create opposing effects: while individual willingness to communicate decreases due to free-riding incentives, communication occurs more frequently overall, and prices are higher when sufficient firms participate. We find that all-inclusive cartels prove essential for achieving high prices. Our second study discovers that ringleader discrimination policies can backfire by facilitating cartel formation through leading-by-example effects. These findings highlight distinct coordination mechanisms of partial cartels and demonstrate the need for careful antitrust policy design.

title: A Comparison of the Greenhouse Gas Protocol's Corporate Standard to the E-Ledgers Measurement System
affiliations: USC Marshall School of Business

detail.title: A Comparison of the Greenhouse Gas Protocol's Corporate Standard to the E-Ledgers Measurement System
detail.abstract: A necessary step to address the concern that increasing levels of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions are causing climate change is measuring GHG emissions released by organizations. The GHG Protocol Initiative takes a "top-down" view and focuses on responsibility: a business measures emissions created throughout its value chain (i.e., emissions created by suppliers, the firm itself, and customers). In contrast, E-ledgers takes a "bottom-up" approach and focuses on control: a business measures emissions embedded in the products or services it owns and sells (cradle-togate emissions). In addition, the GHG Protocol measurement approach aims at helping the firm understand its sources of emissions and focuses on disclosure, whereas E-ledgers aims at creating a worldwide platform that tracks emissions over borders and across entities at the product level and focuses on accountability. Details on how these different perspectives impact reported emissions are discussed, including where the two approaches overlap and where they differ.

title: Option Signals & AI as Middleware: A New Framework for Intelligence, Financial Decision-Making, and Financing
affiliations: EDDA STOCK FINANCE S.A.S

detail.title: Option Signals & AI as Middleware: A New Framework for Intelligence, Financial Decision-Making, and Financing
detail.abstract: This document presents the unified strategic framework developed by Thierry H. Brutman under the EDDA Stock Invest Corp. structure. It integrates the Option Signal methodology with Forecast Intelligence, BFI (Brutman Flexibility Index), MRI (Model of Reflexive Investment), and Volvas Brain — an orchestration layer that governs decisions across production, inventory, services, and finance. In this extended version, the document introduces the Merchant Tracker as a tool for converting future production and service capacity into immediately financeable assets. A novel extension toward tokenized structured finance is presented, demonstrating how governed option signals can be embedded in tokenized instruments to provide liquidity, automated compliance, and secondary tradability. This work challenges the limitations of classical models (IRR, NAV, Real Options) by building a coherent, reflexive governance system for strategic capital allocation. It offers pathways for integration into private markets, sovereign financing, and tokenized infrastructures, while maintaining compliance with accounting, regulatory, and investor-level governance constraints.

title: Diversity Tokenism
affiliations: Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University and Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Diversity Tokenism
detail.abstract: Using data from over 4,000 Black Lives Matter (BLM) protests across 600 U.S. counties from 2014 to 2021, we examine how BLM activism shapes corporate diversity at different organizational levels. We develop an approach integrating OpenAI's GPT-4 with Chain-of-Thought prompting to classify race and ethnicity. In our validation tests, this method achieves higher accuracy than several tested opensource algorithms. Our main findings are as follows. First, although firms headquartered in protestaffected counties add more Black directors, particularly in larger protests, this gain appears to largely offset the representation of other non-Black minority directors. Second, these board-level shifts do not consistently extend to executives or the general workforce. In contrast, a gap may emerge between a firm's workforce composition and local labor-market demographics, particularly in the representation of Black employees. This pattern is consistent with diversity tokenism, which suggests firms may prioritize high-visibility board appointments and potentially downplay broader, transformative change. Our findings indicate that although board-level diversity gains are highly visible and attract notable public attention, they may not be accompanied by an organization's transformative commitment to company-wide diversity.

title: Is Attention Truly All We Need? An Empirical Study of Asset Pricing in Pretrained RNN Sparse and Global Attention Models
affiliations: University of York

detail.title: Is Attention Truly All We Need? An Empirical Study of Asset Pricing in Pretrained RNN Sparse and Global Attention Models
detail.abstract: This study investigates the pretrained RNN attention models with the mainstream attention mechanisms such as additive attention, Luong's three attentions, global self-attention (Self att) and sliding window sparse attention (Sparse att) for the empirical asset pricing research on top 420 large-cap US stocks. This is the first paper on the large-scale state-of-the-art (SOTA) attention mechanisms applied in the asset pricing context. They overcome the limitations of the traditional machine learning (ML) based asset pricing, such as mis-capturing the temporal dependency and short memory. Moreover, the enforced causal masks in the attention mechanisms address the future data leaking issue ignored by the more advanced attention-based models, such as the classic Transformer. The proposed attention models also consider the temporal sparsity characteristic of asset pricing data and mitigate potential overfitting issues by deploying the simplified model structures. This provides some insights for future empirical economic research. All models are examined in three periods, which cover pre-COVID-19 (mild uptrend), COVID-19 (steep uptrend with a large drawdown) and one year post-COVID-19 (sideways movement with high fluctuations), for testing the stability of these models under extreme market conditions. The study finds that in value-weighted portfolio back testing, Model Self att and Model Sparse att exhibit great capabilities in deriving the absolute returns and hedging downside risks, while they achieve an annualized Sortino ratio of 2.0 and 1.80 respectively in the period with COVID-19. And Model Sparse att performs more stably than Model Self att from the perspective of absolute portfolio returns with respect to the size of stocks' market capitalization.

title: The Philosophy of Gastronomy, from Origins to Modernism—Volume 04: Food, Time, and Place
affiliations: Emory University - Oxford College

detail.title: The Philosophy of Gastronomy, from Origins to Modernism—Volume 04: Food, Time, and Place

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency, commercial or not-for-profit sector.

detail.abstract: The Philosophy of Gastronomy—Volume 04: Food, Time, and Place explores the deep connections between food, history, culture, and philosophy. This volume examines the journey of food through human civilization, from spice and sugar routes to the cultural exchanges shaped by migration. It reflects on the significance of seasonal and local foods, the philosophy of nature, and the rise of futuristic food systems driven by technology and globalization. By weaving together perspectives on art, identity, and sustainability, the book demonstrates how food is more than nourishment—it is a living expression of time, place, and human meaning. This work invites chefs, scholars, and readers alike to engage with gastronomy as a cultural and philosophical lens for understanding the past, present, and future of humanity.

title: Forecasting Crude Oil Spot Prices using a Transformer-Bilstm Architecture with NRBO-Based Hyperpamameter Optimization
affiliations: Chengdu University of Technology, Capital University of Economics and Business, Peking University, Chengdu University of Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Forecasting Crude Oil Spot Prices using a Transformer-Bilstm Architecture with NRBO-Based Hyperpamameter Optimization
detail.abstract: A future vision of global crude oil markets is crucial for market participants and policy makers. However, making an accurate prediction of crude oil prices is always challenging, due to the difficulty in extracting both global and local information from historical price data and optimizing hyperparameter settings of the forecasting framework. In this research, a Transformer-BiLSTM-NRBO forecasting model architecture is proposed to overcome these challenges. First, a Transformer-based feature extraction module is adopted to enhance the capture of global information in the forecasting framework. Then, a BiLSTM-based feature extraction module is used to enhance the capture of local information. Finally, an NRBO algorithm is adopted to optimize the key hyperparameter settings of the previous modules. Experiments conducted on daily Bent and WTI crude oil spot prices from 2013 to 2024 illustrate the robust and outstanding forecasting capability of the proposed method. Research limitations and future directions are given.

title: The Impact of Sanctions on the Oil And Gas Sector: A Historical Retrospective
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Impact of Sanctions on the Oil And Gas Sector: A Historical Retrospective
detail.abstract:
In world history, there are many examples of the imposition of sanctions against individual countries that are major producers of oil or natural gas and for which energy exports are one of the most important or key sources of state budget revenue, respectively, developed countries, when imposing sanctions, pursued the goal of reducing the country's income from energy exports and undermining its economy by banning the purchase of of oil or natural gas.

Iran's oil and gas sector has been repeatedly targeted by sanctions imposed by developed countries since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. This is due to the fact that Iran is the third largest country in the world in terms of oil reserves. Accordingly, oil exports are one of the main revenues of Iran's budget. For the first time, the United States imposed sanctions against Iran's oil and gas industry in 1979, immediately after the victory of the Islamic Revolution in the country. President of the United States J. Carter, due to the seizure of the US Embassy in Tehran in November 1979, issued a decree prohibiting the purchase of oil from Iran by the United States. In 1981, the embargo on the Iranian oil trade was lifted.

In 1987, the President of the United States, R. Reagan passed a decree banning the import of oil from Iran. In 1990, exemptions were introduced for a number of American companies that were allowed to import a certain amount of oil from Iran.

In March 1995, U.S. President Bill Clinton issued a decree blocking the first major deal between American and Iranian oil companies since 1979. For example, the Iranian National Oil Company and the American company Conoco have signed an agreement that they will jointly develop an oil field located off the coast of Iran. In May 1995, the President of the United States issued a decree prohibiting American companies from buying oil from Iran for subsequent sale to third countries and from developing oil and natural gas fields located in Iran.

title: From Micro to Macro: Can Machines Unlock New Real-Time Economic Signals from Firm-Level Accounting Data?
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Economics, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Economics and Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Economics

detail.title: From Micro to Macro: Can Machines Unlock New Real-Time Economic Signals from Firm-Level Accounting Data?
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether machines can unlock new real-time economic signals from firm-level accounting data. We develop the Firm-level Accounting data-based Machine Learning (FAML) framework, which applies machine learning algorithms directly to firm-level corporate financial reports to nowcast aggregate economic output. Unlike "aggregate-then-nowcast" approaches, which average firm-level variables into market or sector aggregates, or "factor-then-nowcast" methods, which extract common factors via dynamic factor models, our FAML method operates on the full set of firm-level accounting variables, retaining the informational detail embedded in firm-level heterogeneity and cross-firm interactions while minimizing information loss. Empirically, the FAML framework reduces root mean squared error by over 70% relative to a random walk benchmark and consistently outperforms both aggregation- and factor-based methods. Variable importance analysis further shows that accounting data from the industrials, utilities, and consumer discretionary sectors are particularly informative for economic output nowcasting. These findings underscore the value of leveraging machine learning to transform micro-level accounting data into timely macroeconomic insights.

title: Trade -Growth Nexus in Nepal: A Gravity Model Approach
affiliations: Tribhuvan University and Tribhuvan University

detail.title: Trade -Growth Nexus in Nepal: A Gravity Model Approach
detail.abstract: Purpose of the Study: This study investigates the relationship between trade and economic growth in Nepal, focusing on how factors such as GDP, population, and geographical distance affect Nepal's exports and imports. The research question addresses: "How do these factors influence Nepal's trade dynamics?" Methods/Design: A gravity model framework was used, with panel data analysis employing fixed and random effects models. The Hausman test determined the appropriate model. Data on trade partners' GDP, population, and geographical distance were collected to estimate the model. Findings: The analysis shows that Nepal's exports are positively influenced by the GDP and population of trade partners, while geographical distance negatively impacts trade. Closer countries are more favorable trading partners. The random effects model proved to be the most appropriate estimator, with both the export and import models demonstrating strong explanatory power. Conclusion/Implications: The findings suggest that Nepal should focus on export diversification and strengthen regional trade relations to foster economic growth. Policymakers can use these insights to improve trade strategies and regional cooperation. Limitations of the Study: The study is limited by data constraints and does not account for informal trade flows, which could affect the results. Originality of the Study: This study uniquely applies the gravity model to Nepal's trade context, addressing challenges faced by landlocked developing countries.

title: India-EU Linkages: Green Deal Trade Impacts, Migration Narratives, and Education Diplomacy
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: India-EU Linkages: Green Deal Trade Impacts, Migration Narratives, and Education Diplomacy
detail.abstract: The India-EU partnership is increasingly defined by overlapping challenges in climate, mobility, and education. The European Green Deal, particularly the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), introduces new complexities in India's trade with Europe by targeting carbon-intensive sectors. While the macroeconomic exposure is limited, the sectoral impact on India's iron and steel exports is significant, requiring shifts in compliance, energy efficiency, and diplomatic negotiation. Parallel to trade, migration narratives in both regions diverge sharply: Europe frames migration as a question of regulation and security, while India views it as a developmental and remittance-driven opportunity. These differences shape policy cooperation and public perception. A less explored but equally powerful linkage is education diplomacy, exemplified by Erasmus Mundus programs, which act as soft power channels embedding European values in South Asia's academic and professional networks. This paper examines these three dimensions trade, migration, and education arguing that they together illustrate both the promise and the friction in India-EU relations. By combining economic data, policy discourse, and soft power analysis, the paper highlights how sustainable convergence can only be achieved if trade negotiations are coupled with mutual recognition of migration priorities and deeper academic collaboration.

title: NoLBERT: A No Lookahead(back) Foundational Language Model for Empirical Research
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley and University of California, Berkeley - Haas School of Business

detail.title: NoLBERT: A No Lookahead(back) Foundational Language Model for Empirical Research
detail.abstract: We present NoLBERT, a lightweight, timestamped foundational language model for empirical research in social sciences, particularly in economics and finance. By pre-training exclusively on 1976-1995 text, NoLBERT avoids both lookback and lookahead biases that can undermine econometric inference. It exceeds domain-specific baselines on NLP benchmarks while maintaining temporal consistency. Applied to patent texts, NoLBERT enables the construction of firm-level innovation networks and shows that gains in innovation centrality predict higher long-run profit growth.

title: Comparative Multidimensional Assessment of Progress Towards Sustainability at the Macro Scale: The Cases of 12 OECD Countries, China, and Brazil
affiliations: Environment Europe Foundation

detail.title: Comparative Multidimensional Assessment of Progress Towards Sustainability at the Macro Scale: The Cases of 12 OECD Countries, China, and Brazil
detail.abstract: An assessment of sustainability at the macro level is carried out for 12 leading OECD economies, plus China and Brazil, over the period of 1960-2015 in a comparative dynamic fashion under varying policy priorities: economic, social, environmental, and equal importance. Overall, Sweden, Switzerland, and Norway are found to be outperforming most other countries based on the basket of 16 different sustainability indicators consistently over time. While there are underlying causes of such performance expressed in policies of innovation, decarbonisation, and social cohesion, addressing economic, environmental, and social dimensions, there are some soft factors traditionally lying outside economic or policy domains. Such factors represent the power of institutions, the level of psychological well-being, and societal values, which tend to be statistically different in Sweden, Switzerland, and Norway, as opposed to other countries in the sample. The reasons for the changes in sustainability performance among countries under different policy priorities are discussed at length, with special attention paid to an economically, environmentally, and socially weighted sustainability index of progress.

title: Invisible Engines: Informality, Credit, and Consumption at the Base of the Pyramid in Brazil
affiliations: Independent Researcher and Universidade Unigranrio

detail.title: Invisible Engines: Informality, Credit, and Consumption at the Base of the Pyramid in Brazil
detail.abstract: This article examines how informal financial practices, community-based credit systems, and digital payment innovations (such as Brazil's Pix) shape the economic lives of lowincome populations. Building on empirical observations and theoretical insights, it highlights the paradoxical role of informality: both a survival mechanism and a barrier to full financial inclusion. By analyzing household credit practices, consumption behaviors, and the diffusion of fintech in marginalized communities, the article argues that informality is not merely an economic residue but an invisible engine that sustains the base of the pyramid. Policy recommendations include integrating community-led practices into formal banking strategies and reassessing regulatory frameworks to foster inclusive growth.

title: Investigating the Impact of Cross-Border Shopping Accessibility on Housing Rents: A Case Study of HK Residents' Flocking North
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong - Department of Urban Planning and Design

detail.title: Investigating the Impact of Cross-Border Shopping Accessibility on Housing Rents: A Case Study of HK Residents' Flocking North

declarations.funderStatement: This first draft of this research has received support from the URC Seed Fund for Basic Research for New Staff and the Start-up Fund from The University of Hong Kong (HKU). Its revision process and final publication also received support from the Guangdong Natural Science Fund 2025 - General Programme (External project reference # 2025A1515011085) entitled "How to Maintain GBA's Competency in the New Spatial Equilibrium Paradigm: the Role of Livability in Mainland-HK Population Inflow Tendency and Intensity Under the Post-COVID Lifestyle Preference Shifts" (260842182).

detail.abstract: Since the reopening of border in 2023, Hong Kong (HK) residents are flocking north for weekends due to the high cost-performance commercial offerings in Shenzhen. This study investigates to what extent the accessibility to Shenzhen commercial spaces affects HK's housing rents. Difference-inDifferences (DID) method was utilized to infer the marginal implicit price of crossborder accessibility in the HK rental market. Treatment houses within 34km of border crossings enjoyed ~3.51 HK$/ft 2 extra rent increase, confirming the positive and non-linear net effect of cross-border accessibility. One standard deviation increase in accessibility was related to ~0.65 HK$/ft 2 extra rent increase, of which the magnitude ranked only second to floor (height) and number of rooms. Therefore, the convenience of shopping in Shenzhen have become a nonnegligible factor appreciated by certain HK households when renting houses. The traditionally less-preferred residential areas have gained increased demand, indicating that when interregional economic ties become close, the impact of cross-border accessibility on real estate market in neighboring cities can be strong. Our timely findings offer useful reference to inform interregional policies and transportation infrastructure investment that foster economic integration while accounting for the consequent spillover effects to local markets.

title: Trickle-Up Economics: How Stock Buybacks Exacerbate Wealth Inequality and Health Disparities
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Trickle-Up Economics: How Stock Buybacks Exacerbate Wealth Inequality and Health Disparities
detail.abstract: This paper examines the mechanism of stock buybacks in modern capitalism, illustrating how they facilitate the transfer of wealth from consumers and taxpayers to the wealthiest individuals and corporations. Drawing on historical data, empirical evidence, and case studies from industries such as consumer goods and pharmaceuticals, we demonstrate that stock buybacks, legalized in 1982, inflate stock prices primarily benefiting the top 1% who own over 50% of U.S. equities. We explore the links to CEO compensation, racial disparities in stock ownership, and broader health outcomes, arguing that this system perpetuates inequality. Policy recommendations include supporting small businesses and reconsidering buyback regulations to foster equitable economic cycles.

title: Regulatory Leakage Among Financial Advisors: Evidence From FINRA Regulation of "Bad" Brokers
affiliations: Stanford Law School, University of Virginia - School of Law and New York University School of Law

detail.title: Regulatory Leakage Among Financial Advisors: Evidence From FINRA Regulation of "Bad" Brokers
detail.abstract: The regulatory framework for financial advisors is fragmented, with multiple state and federal regulators. Prior empirical literature on financial advisors has largely focused on a single subset of financial advisors, but we create a database containing brokers regulated primarily by FINRA, investment advisers regulated by the SEC or state securities regulators, and insurance producers regulated by state insurance regulators. There is significant overlap across the regimes; more than 40% of the advisors in our data are registered with more than one regulator. This overlap has implications for labor allocation and market discipline. For example, of the individuals who exit FINRA’s broker regime, 79% were jointly registered in insurance upon exiting FINRA’s regime. This could be efficient if it reflects bad actors who transition to lower risk work, but our evidence shows that these advisors continue to engage in financial planning after they move to the insurance side, as over 90% maintain licenses to sell annuities. Moreover, those who committed misconduct when regulated by FINRA continue to have heightened levels of misconduct in insurance. Our findings have additional implications for regulatory discipline. In 2018 and 2019, FINRA proposed rules designed to nudge “bad” brokers out of the industry. We show that these proposals caused thousands of high-risk brokers to exit the FINRA broker regime, but that the majority of these individuals did not leave financial services—98% are currently registered with state regulators as insurance producers.

title: Cryptocurrencies and Prosperity: Rethinking Development Beyond Fiat Money
affiliations: Universidad Francisco Marroquin - Business School

detail.title: Cryptocurrencies and Prosperity: Rethinking Development Beyond Fiat Money
detail.abstract: This article examines the contrast between two sets of countries: those that illustrate the destruction of prosperity under fiat monetary systems, where governments erode purchasing power and drive inflation that ultimately results in poverty, and those that illustrate the adoption of cryptocurrencies as an alternative. In the case of El Salvador, adoption has been driven by a government-led vision aimed at adding value and fostering innovation, whereas in Nigeria adoption has been driven from the bottom up, as citizens embraced cryptocurrencies out of necessity to hedge against inflation and currency devaluation. The article compares both experiences while engaging with the broader literature on prosperity, monetary systems, and cryptocurrency adoption. It further discusses which processes may be most appropriate for managing future crypto adoption in a way that balances financial stability, inclusion, and long-term development.

title: Leveraging the Capabilities of Multinational Firms to Address Climate Change: A Finance Perspective
affiliations: Imperial College London, University of Alberta, Imperial College London and Swiss Finance Institute

detail.title: Leveraging the Capabilities of Multinational Firms to Address Climate Change: A Finance Perspective
detail.abstract: Climate change and the associated issue of curbing carbon emissions has risen on the agenda of policymakers worldwide. However, global coordination on matters such as harmonized regulation has been subject to significant political frictions and the large intergovernmental transfers needed to finance the transition of developing economies have proven hard to raise. Recently, there have been considerable responses to climate change from the private sector, with stakeholders placing more pressure on firms, and financial markets mobilizing increasing more capital towards the reduction of negative externalities. We argue that although multinational enterprises (MNEs) have been a major contributor to the problem, they can be an important part of the solution-they have unique features that enable them to play an important role in the fight against climate change. MNEs have extensive and efficient internal markets for governance, financing and technology, that enable them to circumvent country-specific frictions to climate action such as heterogeneous regulation, corruption, and the lack of technology. We analyze how different public and private incentive mechanisms could be designed to leverage MNEs' unique features, realign their incentives and engage their potential to play a role in decarbonizing the economy. Lastly, we discuss challenges, opportunities and future research.

title: Political Belief Disagreement: Evidence from IPO Pricing and Share Allocations
affiliations: University of Iowa - Department of Finance

detail.title: Political Belief Disagreement: Evidence from IPO Pricing and Share Allocations
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of political belief disagreement in the IPO setting. By matching IPO deal data with BoardEx executives, institutional holdings data, and political donation records from the FEC, I find that partisan alignment between key participants systematically affects IPO outcomes. Consistent with signaling and overconfidence theories, political misalignment between issuing firm executives and the incumbent president is negatively associated with underpricing. Second, greater partisan disagreement between issuing firm executives and their underwriters predicts higher underpricing, supporting a classic conflict-of-interest channel. Finally, among underwriters and institutional investors, political disagreement is associated with both lower underpricing and smaller share allocations, consistent with a favoritism mechanism in the book-building process. Overall, these findings provide novel evidence that political homophily acts as a key social mechanism influencing IPO pricing and allocation decisions.

title:
Research Fund for Coal and Steel

A summary of the Findings of the Steel Research Technical Groups – 2024
affiliations: European Commission - Joint Research Centre (JRC), European Commission, European Commission, European Commission, European Commission and European Commission

detail.title:
Research Fund for Coal and Steel

A summary of the Findings of the Steel Research Technical Groups – 2024

declarations.funderStatement: European Union

detail.abstract: The 2024 assessments of the RFCS Technical Groups (TGA1–TGA5) confirm the steel sector’s critical role in achieving EU climate and industrial goals. Projects demonstrate strong alignment with the European Green Deal and Clean Steel Partnership, advancing decarbonisation, circularity, and digitalisation. Key achievements include hydrogen-based steelmaking, smart factories, and advanced steel grades for renewables and mobility. However, critical research gaps persist as low-TRL innovation is underfunded, casting and scrap quality need deeper focus, and hydrogen-compatible materials and standards remain underdeveloped. Workforce upskilling, regulatory harmonisation, and lifecycle-based design are essential to scale innovations. Future RFCS calls must balance high-risk research with industrial deployment, foster cross-sector collaboration, and ensure policy alignment. A strategic shift is needed to accelerate the transition to a competitive, climate-neutral, and resilient European steel industry.

title: Portfolio Choice with Target Horizon *

detail.title: Portfolio Choice with Target Horizon *
detail.abstract: I propose a new approach to multi-period portfolio choice that learns about the important aspects of distribution of compounded returns and is suitable for realistic applications where the number of assets is large. I characterize optimal payoffs through systematic factors of compounded asset returns over investors' target horizons and form monthly factor-tracking portfolios that replicate these horizon-specific payoffs. The resulting optimal portfolio is a utility-maximizing combination of the factor-tracking portfolios. The empirical results show economically large utility gains for investors compared to important benchmarks, both in-sample and out-of-sample. More importantly, the estimated portfolio rules are horizon-specific: a multi-period investor benefits from following a horizon-matched rule rather than the rules estimated for alternative horizons. The findings provide compelling evidence for the economic value of investment horizon in portfolio decisions that has been empirically elusive in prior studies.

title: The Market Value of Fed Independence: High-Frequency Evidence from a Natural Experiment
affiliations: Babson College and Babson College - Finance Division

detail.title: The Market Value of Fed Independence: High-Frequency Evidence from a Natural Experiment
detail.abstract: We study how financial markets price threats to Federal Reserve independence by analyzing one of the most direct challenges to Chair Powell’s tenure on July 16, 2025. Following media reports of escalating efforts to dismiss him, prediction markets sharply repriced dismissal risk within a two-hour window, creating a unique high-frequency setting to estimate market responses. Regression estimates imply that the certainty of Powell’s dismissal could erase $0.88–1.51 trillion in total market capitalization. Losses were larger for financial and credit-dependent firms, consistent with the credit channel of monetary policy transmission, and for high-beta firms. Treasury yields declined at short maturities but increased at longer horizons, steepening the yield curve, while the dollar depreciated against major currencies. These results show that markets price not only near-term policy-rate expectations but also the Federal Reserve’s ability to act independently.

title: AdaSwitch: An Adaptive Switching Meta-Algorithm for Learning-Augmented Bounded-Influence Problems
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business,  and Tsinghua University - Yau Mathematical Sciences Center

detail.title: AdaSwitch: An Adaptive Switching Meta-Algorithm for Learning-Augmented Bounded-Influence Problems
detail.abstract: We study a class of multi-period online decision-making problems with sequence-based predictions, which may be generated by machine learning models but whose accuracy is not guaranteed. In each period, the decision-maker observes the realized request and must take an irrevocable action that yields a reward or incurs a cost, without knowledge of future arrivals. We introduce a bounded-influence framework, in which past decisions and requests exert only limited impact on the future optimal reward. Within this framework, we propose the AdaSwitch meta-algorithm, which exploits predictions to attain performance close to the offline benchmark when predictions are accurate, while preserving classical competitive-ratio guarantees under highly inaccurate predictions. Our framework and meta-algorithm apply to diverse settings, including lead-time quotation in processing systems, the k-server problem, and online allocation of reusable resources. These applications illustrate the flexibility and broad applicability of our approach to learning-augmented online decision-making.

title: Taxation of Gambling After the OBBBA
affiliations: Texas Tech University School of Law

detail.title: Taxation of Gambling After the OBBBA

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship with any person or organization related to my paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: Texas Tech University School of Law

detail.abstract:
In the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, P.L. 119-21), Congress rewrote section 165(d), the section that both permits and restricts deductions arising from gambling losses. 

This article explores the nuances of the Congressional revision to section 165(d).  It first explains the two main problems with the former section: (1) a structural problem that forced taxpayers to report phantom income; and (2) an accounting problem about how taxpayers were supposed to net gambling wins with gambling losses.  It then analyzes the OBBBA revisions to show how they exacerbates the structural problem but potentially resolve the netting problem in a taxpayer-friendly manner. 

The article concludes with reviewing best practices for both advising and representing gamblers before the IRS and in court.

title: Exogenous Social Norms Drive Fisheries Compliance in the Absence of Adequate Enforcement: Insights from a Novel Experimental Game
affiliations: James Cook University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Sydney, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Exogenous Social Norms Drive Fisheries Compliance in the Absence of Adequate Enforcement: Insights from a Novel Experimental Game
detail.abstract: Compliance with rules and laws is critical to societal function and may be driven more by social pressures than enforcement penalties. In conservation, many protected areas closed to hunting and fishing have been rendered ineffective due to inadequate compliance. Here, we explore the role of social norms in compliance decisions by using a novel experimental game to study real anglers’ decisions to fish ‘illegally’ in a simulated marine protected area (MPA) or ‘legally’ in an open access fishing ground. We demonstrate that a descriptive social norm, exogenously created by computer confederates posing as other players, can increase or decrease compliance over time, as participants conformed to confederate decisions even though these were irrelevant to their final payouts. Results build on past common pool resource games studying cooperation as a viable long-term strategy in fisheries, showing how cooperative (or non-cooperative) behaviors can be driven by conformity to group norms. Additionally, we developed a model to predict participants’ compliance decisions, which revealed that normative influence accumulated, such that each rulebreaker observed over time makes individuals more likely to eventually break the rules themselves. Noncompliance was also more likely after losses due to poor catch, but being caught and fined had a weaker influence on rulebreakers than catch or norms, suggesting a ‘resetting effect’ where apprehended rulebreakers believed future fines were now less likely.

title: Ecological Debt Swaps for a Twin Debt Justice
affiliations: University of Rome Tor Vergata - Faculty of Economics, University of Tuscia and Athens University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Ecological Debt Swaps for a Twin Debt Justice

declarations.ethicsApproval: The paper does not use own empirical data

detail.abstract: We explore the intersection of foreign debt in poor and emerging countries and global climate challenges, proposing a novel debt of "ecological debt swap" to promote both financial and ecological debt sustainability. We sketch the main characteristics of a comprehensive ecological debt swap scheme involving multiple stakeholders, including international development banks, private sector actors pursuing net-zero targets, and local communities. Under this scheme, debt relief would be conditional upon investments in renewable energy projects and sustainability initiatives in debtor countries. A main advantage of the swap over the alternative of unconditional debt relief accompanied by lender subsidized green finance is that the former has features that are mutually beneficial for the counterparts easing the participation constraint of the lender, preventing green moral hazard of the borrower and increasing efficiency in emission reduction. We as well show that related climate investments could reduce global carbon emissions, promote local economic resilience, and address energy poverty.

title: Multidimensional Sustainability Assessment for Megacities
affiliations: Environment Europe Foundation

detail.title: Multidimensional Sustainability Assessment for Megacities
detail.abstract: Urban sustainability assessment is required for the purposes of establishing strategic directions for ‘greening’ our cities to reduce the environmental impact of their performance, improve employment and economic viability and enhance the quality of life. This chapter considers large world cities: London, New York, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, Sao Paolo, Rio de Janeiro, Paris, Berlin, Singapore, Shanghai, Sydney and Tokyo. To assess urban sustainability performance, we applied multicriteria decision aid tools to compare the cities on the range of dimensions. The tools chosen for this assessment are ELECTRE III, NAIADE and APIS. The results have shown that Singapore dominates the sustainability rankings in most multicriteria applications, showing particular strength in economic and environmental dimensions and a slightly less strong performance in the social dimension according to the APIS results. The chapter explores innovative sustainability strategy and new governance structures in Singapore and discusses the reasons for such success.

title: Optimal Taxation under Imperfect Trust
affiliations: , Independent and National Research University Higher School of Economics (Moscow) - International College of Economics and Finance

detail.title: Optimal Taxation under Imperfect Trust
detail.abstract: We study optimal taxation when the conversion of tax revenue into public goods is uncertain. In a static Ramsey framework with a representative household, a competitive firm, and two broad instruments (a labor-income tax and a commodity/output tax), a simple measure of trust-the perceived likelihood that revenue is actually delivered as public consumption-scales the marginal value of public funds. We show: (i) a trust threshold below which any distortionary taxation reduces welfare; (ii) above that threshold, policy uniquely pins down the scale of taxation but leaves a continuum of tax mixes (an equivalence frontier) that implement the same allocation and welfare; and (iii) tiny administrative or salience wedges select a unique instrument, typically favoring a broad base collected at source. We derive a trust-adjusted Ramsey rule in sufficient-statistics form, establish robustness to mild preference non-separabilities and concave public-good utility, and provide an isoelastic specialization with transparent comparative statics.

title: Crossroads of Peace: Advancing Regional Integration and Global Trade Through Post-Conflict Cooperation
affiliations: Armenian State University of Economics, Yerevan and

detail.title: Crossroads of Peace: Advancing Regional Integration and Global Trade Through Post-Conflict Cooperation

The authors affirm that their affiliation did not influence the design, conduct, analysis, or reporting of this study. The views expressed in this article are solely those of the authors and do not necessarily represent the official position of the Ministry of Economy or the Government of the Republic of Armenia.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This article does not contain any studies with human participants performed by any of the authors. This article does not contain any studies with animals performed by any authors
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded through an honorarium provided by the Armenian State University of Economics.

detail.abstract: This article examines the potential economic benefits of the Crossroads of Peace (CoP) initiative proposed by the Government of Armenia. To assess regional trade dynamics, three indicators were applied: the Export Similarity Index (ESI), the Trade Complementarity Index (TCI), and the Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA). The findings reveal that the ESI between Armenia and its regional partners, Türkiye and Azerbaijan, is 0.25, indicating minimal competition in export markets. In contrast, the TCI score of 0.5 from the region to Armenia suggests a relatively higher degree of complementarity, highlighting stronger opportunities for regional exports to Armenia than vice versa. Furthermore, Armenia's projected trade volume with Türkiye in 2024 is estimated at USD 787 million, underscoring the initiative's potential to foster significant economic exchange.

title: Natural Capital and Economic Growth
affiliations: , Amundi Asset Management and Amundi Asset Management

detail.title: Natural Capital and Economic Growth
detail.abstract: This paper examines the complex relationship between natural capital and longterm economic growth. Specifically, we review resource-based growth theories and various modeling approaches. In most frameworks, natural capital is considered an additional production factor that supplements traditional inputs. However, we highlight a common conceptual confusion between economic wealth (a stock) and economic growth (a flow). This distinction is often overlooked in discussions about the role of natural assets in development. Using World Bank data from 1995 to 2020, we empirically estimate a Cobb-Douglas production function that incorporates produced (physical) capital, labor (human capital), renewable resources, and non-renewable resources. We then classify countries according to their resource endowment and assess the elasticity of natural capital with respect to GDP. To address uncertainty and downside risk, we propose a stress-testing framework that integrates historical worst-case analysis, parametric methods, and extreme value theory. Our results reveal significant heterogeneity in the impact of natural capital on growth. Over the past 25 years, non-renewable resources appear to have had little influence on economic growth. Conversely, growth has been more responsive to renewable resources. Notably, countries such as Iran, Australia, South Korea, and Nicaragua experienced a negative contribution of natural capital to growth, while Vietnam, Indonesia, Mozambique, and Egypt experienced a positive contribution. The stress-testing analysis further underscores wide crosscountry variation. Over a 25-year horizon, the countries that are potentially most affected by adverse natural capital scenarios include Ethiopia, Chile, New Zealand, Brazil, Iran, and Poland. An additional insight comes from decomposing the stress test results into the sum of the worst-performing years. This reveals that, in some countries, stress outcomes are driven by one or two severe events. In contrast, in other countries, a prolonged decline in natural capital leads to multiple moderately bad years without any single catastrophic event.

title: Peer Effects in Old-Age Employment Among Women
affiliations: Charles University in Prague - CERGE-EI, a joint workplace of Charles University and the Economics Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences

detail.title: Peer Effects in Old-Age Employment Among Women

declarations.funderStatement: This study was supported by Charles University, GAUK project No. 333221.

detail.abstract: This paper exploits a unique norm-shifting setting-a German pension reform that equalized retirement ages across genders-to examine how old-age employment propagates through workplace networks. The reform raised women's earliest claiming age from 60 to 63 for cohorts born in 1952 onward. Using the universe of workgroups from social security records, I compare women whose peers were just above or below the reform cutoff. I find that women are more likely to remain employed at older ages when their peers do, with stronger effects in the regions of former West Germany, with its traditional gender norms. Gender-neutral pension reforms thus amplify their impact through peer influence, fostering regional convergence in late-career employment patterns.

title: Comparative Sustainability Analysis of Two Asian Cities: A Multidimensional Assessment of Taipei and Almaty
affiliations: Environment Europe Foundation, Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, Sarsen Amanzholov East Kazakhstan State University and ITMO University

detail.title: Comparative Sustainability Analysis of Two Asian Cities: A Multidimensional Assessment of Taipei and Almaty
detail.abstract: The article compares economic and environmental performance of Taipei and Almaty from the point of view of "green" economy, which is able to act as a key tool to ensure sustainable development of the region. As the comparison of the parameters of ecological and economic development of the Taipei and Almaty cities shows, they are similar in population size, but demonstrate completely different trends of sustainable development. Economic performance of the Taipei city is achieved with a decrease in the consumption of natural resources and the production of pollution, while the situation in Almaty is the opposite. Almaty maintains a high level of air pollution due to the use of coal in electricity production, as well as increased traffic and density of construction, including the southern part of the city, which is a zone for the transit of mountain air flows. The article discusses the activities jointly conducted by the Government of Taiwan and non-governmental organizations on environmental issues, as well as environmental NGOs, which resulted in significant improvements in the environmental field. Measures to stimulate the development and implementation of environmental innovations applied in the field of sustainable development in the city of Taipei can be adapted for the city of Almaty, where the environmental situation deteriorates year by year.

title: Long-Term Effects of Economic Growth and Unemployment on Caloric Intake: An Empirical Analysis With ARDL Modeling in the United States (1961–2018)
affiliations: Baku State University, Baku State University, Baku State University and Baku State University

detail.title: Long-Term Effects of Economic Growth and Unemployment on Caloric Intake: An Empirical Analysis With ARDL Modeling in the United States (1961–2018)
detail.abstract: This study investigates the long-term effects of economic growth and unemployment on per capita caloric intake in the United States from 1961 to 2018. Using data obtained from the U.S. Bureau of Statistics, we employ an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to analyze the relationship between caloric consumption, GDP per capita, and unemployment rates. The study first conducts unit root tests to determine the stationarity of the time series data, followed by the application of the ARDL model to identify long-term equilibrium relationships among the variables. The results indicate a significant positive relationship between GDP per capita and caloric intake, while unemployment shows a negative impact on caloric consumption. The findings underscore the importance of economic stability and growth in improving dietary habits and overall public health. Policy implications suggest that efforts to reduce unemployment and promote economic growth can have beneficial effects on population health and nutrition.

reference: Revista Direito e Práxis, Rio de Janeiro, volume 13, issue 4, 2022, p. 2648-2686.
title: Digital Constitutionalism: Contradictions of a Loose Concept
affiliations: Rio de Janeiro State University and WZB Berlin Social Science Center

detail.title: Digital Constitutionalism: Contradictions of a Loose Concept

publicationDetails.detailsText: Revista Direito e Práxis, Rio de Janeiro, volume 13, issue 4, 2022, p. 2648-2686.

detail.abstract: This paper maps the uses of the expression digital constitutionalism, as employed in recent debates about digital technologies regulation (in particular, digital platforms). Our goal is to highlight discrepancies and risks implied in the dilatation of the term "constitutionalism" to encompass the normative phenomena that run under this label. In light of the understanding of traditional constitutionalism as a political and institutional phenomenon, we identify the theories that precede digital constitutionalism as contemporary formulations aimed at explaining changes in the functioning of powers and normative systems that transcend or overlap the nation-state and its territorial boundaries (i.e., constitutional pluralism, societal constitutionalism, and global constitutionalism). Based on the literature's criticism of this theoretical matrix, digital constitutionalism is problematized as a term epistemically impaired by the diversity of applications and the potential to legitimize concentrations of private powers.

title: On Empirical Validation of Marginal Build Emissions Rates
affiliations: WattTime, WattTime and WattTime

detail.title: On Empirical Validation of Marginal Build Emissions Rates
detail.abstract: The Greenhouse Gas Protocol Protocol (GHGP) proposes that the long-run marginal emissions rate (LRMER) of the power grid can be captured by a combination of the Marginal Operating Emissions Rate (MOER) and the Marginal Build Emissions Rate (MBER) with a build margin weight (w). This approach has largely been untested against realworld conditions. In this study, we demonstrate a two-step method to empirically validate this methodology. In the first step, we leveraged the fact that all known MBER modeling approaches rely on making predictions of future capacity growth. By measuring the accuracy of this prediction using actual historical capacity growth, we are able to perform a validation test for MBER models that is empirical, and does not rely on any unobservable counterfactual. In the second step, we use the actual historical changes in emissions associated with past natural variations in load to evaluate the ability of an MBER model with a given value of w to produce accurate LRMER values. As a proof-of-concept, we examine two implementations of MBER and the methodology described in the current Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP) using their default generic build weight of w = 1/2. We compared this model's performance in producing accurate MBERs and LRMERs in grid regions across the continental United States, and found that it has significant ability to successfully predict power plant build by fuel type and estimate LRMER values. We also found that a weight parameter of w = 1/2 to be more consistent with the empirical LRMER than models that are purely MOER or purely MBER.

title: An Analysis of Legal Realism's Influence on Modern Dispute Resolution Practices
affiliations: University of the Punjab , Jhelum Campus

detail.title: An Analysis of Legal Realism's Influence on Modern Dispute Resolution Practices
detail.abstract: Legal realism as a jurisprudence movement has substantially transformed the modern jurisprudence of dispute resolution by discrediting the formalistic foundations of law and advocating the practical and contextual solutions. This research explores the influence of legal realism on progress and application of ADR methods (negotiation, mediation and arbitration). Bypassing the rigidity of the traditional adjudication, legal realism has shifted towards interest-based negotiation as compared to the rights-based negotiation which is more cooperative and result-oriented. Realism has changed the mediator role as problem solving and empathetic as opposed to advocacy in an adversary process and systemic reforms that are increasingly promoting the use of mediation over formal litigation. Procedural flexibility in arbitration can consider legal requirements and fair considerations to balance. The study uses empirical research and comparative legal research and evaluates the success of the realist-inspired ADR practices that are quantifiable and their cross-cultural adaptability. Legal realism makes dispute resolution more efficient, fairer, and a more whole-person, multi-dimensional attitude to resolve conflicts. However, some challenges exist in regards to standardizing the practices in different jurisdictions with different traditions of law. Current study reiterates on the ever-present implications of legal realism on the modern day dispute resolution and highlight the aspects of potential future reforms.

title: Copyright and the Dynamics of Innovation in Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: University of Lausanne - Faculty of Business and Economics (HEC Lausanne)

detail.title: Copyright and the Dynamics of Innovation in Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: Copyright can determine access to data, which may, in turn, affect innovation in Artificial Intelligence (AI). In this paper, we conduct an empirical analysis to investigate the relationship between copyright and the dynamics of AI innovation. Some countries provide exceptions in copyright law that are relevant for AI, particularly concerning text and data mining and the doctrine of fair use. The study takes a global perspective, comparing different countries based on the breadth of exceptions in copyright law. We find that countries with broader copyright exceptions tend to exhibit higher levels of AI innovation, as measured in a larger number of AI research publications, more active participation in open-source AI projects, increased AI patent filings, and a higher rate of AI venture formation. These findings suggest that statutory provisions enabling data access can be pivotal in fostering AI innovation. However, while broad copyright exceptions may support current AI innovation by allowing the use of existing works, they might also inadvertently discourage the creation of new works, leading to negative long-term consequences for the availability and quality of training data.
